# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**My top pick is the JBL Charge 6.** It has an IP68 rating, 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost) and 40W of power. It also works as a power bank for your phone. What Hi-Fi named it best overall, and Best Products did too. Prices run about $130 at Walmart to $150 at Amazon. [Retailer links on What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)

## Other picks by need

- **Best for a pool party: JBL Boombox 4.** RTINGS ranks it the best waterproof speaker it has tested. It floats, handles long immersion, gets loud, and lasts over 40 hours. It's big and expensive, and it sounds muffled if you're beside or behind it. [RTINGS review and retailer links](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)
- **Best 360° sound that floats: Ultimate Ears Epicboom.** It's IP67, floats, and sounds the same from every side. Battery is about 15 hours. Tom's Guide picked it as best overall and RTINGS as best mid-range. [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)
- **Best budget: Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4.** It's IP67, floats, and lasts about 14 hours. Best Products listed it at $65, down from $80. [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)
- **Cheapest: JBL Go 5.** It's IP67 and pocket-sized, but battery is only about 8 hours. It was $39.95 at Amazon. [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)
- **Best to carry: JBL Grip.** It's about $100, IP68, under a pound, and shaped like a can, so it fits in a bag's bottle pocket. Good Housekeeping's DJ tester picked it as best overall. Battery is 12 hours. [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)

## Soundcore options with a discount code

Dealectric tested these codes in Soundcore's own cart on Oct 22. Dealectric earns a commission on purchases through its links, at no cost to you. Enter the code at checkout, and Soundcore's checkout has the final word on price.

- [Soundcore Boom 3i Rugged Waterproof Speaker](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-3i): $129.99, or $104 with code **AFSC20**
- [Soundcore Boom 2 Plus Outdoor Speaker](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus): $249.99, or $200 with code **AFSC20**

The sources I have don't review these two models, so I can't vouch for their sound. Best Products did praise the earlier Soundcore Boom 2 as good value, but it noted that model has no dust rating.

## Tips

- **IP rating:** For the pool or beach, look for IP67 or better. The "6" also helps keep sand out. Tom's Guide and Good Housekeeping both recommend this.
- **Salt and chlorine:** IP ratings don't cover corrosion from salt water or chlorine. RTINGS suggests rinsing the speaker with fresh water after use. Check your model's manual first, since some advise against using it at the beach.
- **Charging port:** Keep the port cover closed and let the speaker dry fully before charging it.
- **Placement:** Keep it on a towel or raised surface rather than buried in sand, and out of direct sun.

I couldn't open retailer pages here, so I linked the review pages that list current retailer prices. Check the price before you buy, since the sources were published at different times.

If you tell me your budget and whether you want something pocketable or party-loud, I can narrow this to one pick.
